source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Custom synthesis and peptides initiatives, supported by a new center of excellence, emerged as key growth engines... due to increased demand from global pharmaceutical companies; company monitors effect of U.S. tariffs on suppliers from China and has expanded sourcing options across regions as a precautionary step (FY25/Q1FY26 commentary)

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports accounted for ~88% of FY25 revenue (Rs 9,712 cr total revenue, up 19% YoY); reported forex gain of Rs 90 cr in a subsequent quarter vs Rs 10 cr prior year, indicating material forex P&L sensitivity

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories does not appear among the firms approved under the Feb 2021 initial PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs (KSM/DI/API); approved list included Aarti Speciality Chemicals, Macleods, Optimus Drugs, Sudarshan Pharma, Saraca Labs, Meghmani and others, not Divi's

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 sales of Rs 520 bn: India Formulations 33% (Rs 169,230 mn, +13.7%), US Formulations 31% (Rs 162,403 mn / US$1,921 mn, +3.6%), Emerging Markets Formulations 18% (Rs 94,160 mn), Rest of World Formulations 14% (Rs 71,626 mn), API & Others 4%

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma does not appear among the approved beneficiary list for the PLI Bulk Drugs (KSM/DI/API) scheme in available search results

govt_capex.evidence: Business mix in India closely linked to government and private-sector capex cycles (railways, metro networks, power transmission, smart cities); Mobility segment (rail electrification, rolling stock, rail automation) described as 'a consistent beneficiary of India's elevated capital expenditure in railways'; order backlog Rs 39,770 cr in FY24 with new orders of Rs 16,630 cr; a ~Rs 13,000 cr locomotive order (post prototype approval) represents about 30% of total order book; CEO noted government capex execution improved from ~40-50% to ~75-85%

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Siemens Ltd India being a selected beneficiary under PLI schemes searched (White Goods PLI beneficiaries are AC/LED manufacturers, not Siemens); Siemens is referenced only as an exporter of transformers within the broader electrical equipment value chain, not as an approved PLI applicant

rural.evidence: Two-wheeler segment demand recovery attributed partly to 'improved rural demand and financing availability following GST cuts'; Royal Enfield growth described as driven 'primarily by strong domestic demand for its sub-350cc motorcycle range'; management expects 'improving rural incomes' to support the sector over the medium term

pli_scheme.evidence: Eicher Motors Limited is listed as an approved applicant under the PLI-Auto 'Champion OEM' category (official approved-applicant list, pliauto.in), alongside Ashok Leyland, Bajaj Auto, Hero MotoCorp, Hyundai Motor India, Mahindra & Mahindra, and Tata Motors

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar is a global supplier with 12 manufacturing/assembly facilities across India, USA, Mexico and China, with over 50% of sales for international markets; company frames its strategy as 'diversifying across products, customers, and geographies' rather than an explicit China+1 sourcing-shift narrative, and in FY25-26 it is actually entering China via a JV (Jinnaite Machinery) rather than diversifying away from it.

govt_capex.evidence: Completed acquisition of Escorts Kubota's Railway Equipment Division (RED) for ~INR 1,660 crore; RED is a 60-year supplier to Indian Railways with IRIS Silver certification for brake systems, recording standalone revenue of INR 913 crore in FY25 (only partially consolidated into Sona's FY25 numbers given deal timing).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Historically near debt-free: long-term debt fell from INR 487mn (FY23) to INR 292mn (FY24) to INR 80mn (FY24-end); borrowings rose to INR 242.69 crore only after the FY25/26 Escorts Kubota acquisition financing.

crude_exposure.evidence: Search commentary cites 'near-term margin pressure driven by product mix toward lower-margin traction motors and recent commodity inflation' (steel/metals, not crude-specific); no company-disclosed raw-material % found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Over 50% of sales are for international markets (North America + Europe combined ~54% of FY25 revenue per geography split above), implying meaningful USD/EUR revenue exposure; no explicit hedging policy disclosure found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian auto-component supplier to receive Auto PLI scheme certification, for a hub wheel drive motor for electric two-wheelers, and has filed seven applications for different products under the scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India describes itself as pursuing a 'local for local' strategy across 23 market segments; exports are described as not a primary strategic focus, with expansion decided by ABB's global divisions based on market needs. No China+1 / supply-chain diversification narrative found.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB secured a major traction order for Mumbai Metro expansion (18 six-car trainsets for Line 6, 22 for Line 5), described by the company as aligned with 'Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat' initiatives; record FY2024-25 Railways capex allocation of INR 2,62,200 crore flows into sectors (railways, T&D, urban infra) where ABB has a dominant presence. Order backlog was INR 9,380 crore as of Dec 31 2024 (+12% YoY), highest-ever orders of INR 13,079 crore for the year.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is widely reported (third-party aggregators) as almost debt-free; no specific floating-rate liability disclosure found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue growth in some quarters attributed partly to 'export markets from Distribution Solution division,' but no quantified export/USD revenue % disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: JBCPL exports to over 30 countries and earns more than 40% of revenue from its international business (Russia, CIS, South Africa, branded generics, CDMO); no explicit China+1 / API-diversification-from-China framing attributed to the company was found (India as a whole still depends on China for ~70% of bulk drug/intermediate imports per industry commentary, not company-specific).

rural.evidence: Company strategy explicitly includes 'increasing penetration in Tier II, Tier III and rural markets'; e.g., the YUVA field force division (Rantac + Metrogyl brands) had ~150 of 600 medical reps (25%) deployed in rural markets. Top 4 brands (Cilacar, Rantac, Metrogyl, Nicardia) account for >85% of domestic formulation sales.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is near debt-free: gross debt was INR 14 crore as of March 31, 2025, down further to INR 7 crore by September 30, 2025.

crude_exposure.evidence: No company-specific raw-material-cost disclosure found; general industry context notes API/solvent costs are petrochemical-derived and sensitive to crude/energy prices, but this was not tied to JBCPL specifically.

inr_exposure.evidence: International business (Russia, CIS, South Africa, branded generics, CDMO exports) was INR 1,649 crore of INR 3,918 crore total FY25 revenue (~42%), implying meaningful multi-currency (not purely USD) exposure; no hedging policy disclosure found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Torrent's FY25 revenue mix (India 55%, Brazil 10%, US 10%, Germany 10%, other markets 15%) reflects a meaningful export business, but no explicit China+1 / API-sourcing-diversification narrative attributable to Torrent specifically was found in available sources.

rural.evidence: Company is expanding field force (>6,800 reps covering 200,000+ doctors, with plans to grow toward 10,000) specifically targeting Tier-2/Tier-3 markets; Tier II and Tier III cities are projected to drive over 40% of domestic pharma sales growth. India revenue was INR 6,393 crore in FY2024-25.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt declined to ~INR 16 billion (FY24) from INR 25 billion (FY23); Debt/Equity ~0.4 and net debt/EBITDA ~0.6 in FY25; interest coverage improved to 7.7x (FY24) from 6.5x (FY23). No specific floating-vs-fixed rate split disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: US market contributed ~10% of FY25 revenue per geography mix; remaining export exposure spread across BRL (Brazil ~10%), EUR (Germany ~10%) and other currencies (~15%), implying diversified rather than purely USD-linked forex exposure. No hedging policy disclosure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Torrent Pharmaceuticals is named as a speciality player in Category 1 of the PLI Pharma scheme (INR 15,000 crore outlay, covering complex-formulation manufacturers and biosimilars developers, incentive window FY2020-21 to FY2025-26).

rate_sensitive.evidence: "The Company does not carry any debt and is not required to obtain a credit rating." / "We are a zero-debt company."

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Hedges trade receivables in major currencies (USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, JPY) via forward contracts to minimize realized FX gain/loss volatility; net unhedged FX exposure disclosed separately.
inr_exposure.evidence: "A substantial portion of the Company's revenue is generated in foreign currencies, while majority of the Company's expenses are incurred in Indian Rupees... The Company hedges the trade receivables in major currencies..." / "The Company's geographic spread offers it a natural hedge against economic slowdown affecting a region."

govt_capex.evidence: "The order-book clientele is well diversified with Government contributing 49%, PSUs with 18% and Private sector with 33% share." Order book also diversified by segment: Marine Structures 31.2%, Urban Infrastructure/Metros/Airports 22%, Highways/Bridges/Cargo 16.8% (order-book mix, not booked-revenue mix; company FY24-25 consolidated revenue ~Rs 9,097 Cr, PAT Rs 373 Cr, up 36%).

inr_exposure.evidence: Executing two overseas orders, one each in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh (marine/port works), plus prior Myanmar presence; overseas revenue share not disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Anthem Biosciences is distinguished by its 'China-plus-one' strategy, having built a supply chain with minimal dependence on Chinese raw materials, sourcing less than 20 percent of its inputs from the country... We're now the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones" (CEO/Founder Ajay Bhardwaj); positioned in IPO materials as a 'China alternative' amid global pharma supply-chain diversification.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributed ~85% of FY2024-25 revenue from operations (~Rs 1,844 Cr / ~INR 18bn total revenue), serving customers across 50 countries; geography split North America 26.42%, Europe 56.61%, Rest of Asia and others 2.41% (IPO prospectus disclosure).

pli_scheme.evidence: Coverage notes rising API/peptide demand could be aided by government's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs and bulk-drug parks as a sector tailwind, but no company-specific disclosure confirming Anthem as an approved PLI beneficiary was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: "This export growth can be attributed to the positive global sentiment towards sourcing from India, fuelled by the China Plus One diversification strategy adopted by many companies" (industry-level MD&A commentary on the Indian auto-component sector, not specifically attributed to Gabriel's own order growth); separately, MD&A notes the company has "slashed imports from China by over half, even as our business grew over 1.5 times" (import-substitution/localisation, not export-driven).

rural.evidence: Only a workforce-location metric is disclosed in the BRSR (not a revenue split): "Rural 66.39% / Semi-urban 12.09% / Urban 21.53%" of wages paid by employee location, FY2023-24.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company itself is near debt-free (Debt/Equity ~0.03); only disclosed floating-rate exposure is at subsidiary level: "Inalfa Gabriel Sunroof Systems Private Limited has availed unsecured short term loan from bank... which carries variable interest linked to 3 months MCLR p.a and 6 months MCLR" (₹251.67 million as at March 31, 2024).

crude_exposure.evidence: "Cost of material consumed" was ₹24,706.30 million against "Revenue from operations" of ₹33,426.48 million (~73.9%) in FY2023-24. "The Company has significant usage of commodities like Steel, Oil, Aluminum exposing it to price risk arising out of market fluctuations... back to back pass through arrangements for volatility in raw material prices there is limited impact on the profit and loss."

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved Forex Policy laying down principles of hedging forex risk; hedges designated as cash flow hedges via foreign exchange forward contracts.
inr_exposure.evidence: "The Company enters into international transactions and is exposed to resultant foreign exchange risk, primarily with respect to the USD, CNH (RMB), EUR and JPY... The objective of the hedges is to minimise the volatility of the INR cash flows of highly probable forecast transactions." Actual export revenue is small (~2.7% of total per geographic segment note), so FX exposure is more import/raw-material-side than revenue-side.

pli_scheme.evidence: AR references the Government's PLI scheme for automobiles/auto components as a sector-level tailwind (e.g., FY25 budget allocation hike) but does not disclose Gabriel India itself as an approved/participating beneficiary.

rural.evidence: Company distributes through 100,000+ retail outlets and 10,000+ on-premise locations across India; industry growth attributed partly to rising disposable incomes in tier-two cities and rural areas, but no company-specific rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt of approx Rs 868 crore as of Mar-25 (up from Rs 749 crore Mar-24); total debt approx Rs 1,000 crore with short-term borrowings of Rs 693 crore; debt/equity 0.36. Floating vs fixed split not found in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: ENA, grain, glass and packaging material prices are called out as key volatile cost drivers; glass bottle and packaging costs (partly crude/petrochemical-linked via PET/caps) rose sharply industry-wide (glass +12-20%, cans +8%+) in recent periods. Exact % of raw material cost tied to crude-linked inputs not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company derives approximately 5-6% of sales volumes and 9-10% of revenue from exports to 100+ countries; no explicit hedging policy disclosure found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI (manufacturing) scheme applicability found for IMFL/spirits; alcohol/liquor is not among the 14 PLI-covered sectors.

china_plus_one.evidence: Pidilite's China exposure is a sales/trading subsidiary (Pidilite Industries Trading (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.) selling into China, not a supply-chain-diversification-away-from-China narrative; no China+1 framing found.

rural.evidence: Management commentary (termed 'Emerging India'): growth in rural markets has outpaced urban growth in recent quarters; exact rural revenue % not disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: MD&A commentary notes the company is 'optimistically cautious about the demand landscape,' citing increased government capex and infrastructure spend as a factor expected to help revive construction-linked (waterproofing/tile-fixing under Dr. Fixit/Roff) demand.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has no outstanding term loans in FY24 or FY25; Debt/Equity ratio is 0.0, indicating an effectively debt-free balance sheet.

crude_exposure.evidence: VAM (Vinyl Acetate Monomer), a petrochemical/crude-derivative, is described as the single biggest raw material input; VAM cost movements are tied to crude oil price trends and materially affect gross margins. Exact % of total raw material cost from VAM/crude-linked inputs not found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributed roughly Rs 993 crore in FY25 revenue with overseas subsidiaries adding a further ~Rs 647 crore (~6.5-7.3% of consolidated revenue from international operations); VAM raw material is also imported (USD-denominated), creating exposure on both revenue and cost sides. Specific hedging/forward-contract policy not found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme participation found; adhesives/specialty chemicals sector is not among India's 14 designated PLI sectors.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL has been net-debt-free since FY22 and remained so through FY25; company reported nil net debt, gross cash position of Rs 3,073 crore as of March 31, 2025, and no significant debt apart from lease liabilities.

crude_exposure.evidence: Hospitality business has minimal direct raw-material/crude linkage (fuel/LPG for kitchen and utilities is a minor, undisclosed cost line); no raw material cost disclosure comparable to a manufacturer was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL (consolidated) reported FY25 revenue of Rs 8,565 crore vs standalone (largely India) revenue of Rs 5,145 crore, implying a meaningful share of consolidated revenue from international/managed hotel operations across 4 continents and 14 countries, but a precise foreign-currency revenue % and hedging policy were not found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Hospitality is not a PLI-covered sector.

china_plus_one.evidence: Integrated Report business review notes Lupin's API and CDMO businesses 'reflected strong alignment with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing, and high-potency APIs,' and that policies like the proposed US Biosecure Act (aimed at reducing dependency on China) are prompting global pharma players to diversify suppliers, with Lupin's India-based API/CDMO operations 'well placed to support this transition.'

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt approx Rs 60.2 billion in FY25, with long-term debt of Rs 18 billion (vs near-nil in FY24); interest coverage improved to 14.6x from 8.8x; finance costs down 5.4% YoY. Fixed vs floating rate breakdown not found in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company uses multi-sourcing, long-term vendor contracts, and local backward integration to manage volatility in API and Key Starting Material (KSM) pricing, many of which are petrochemical-derived; exact % of raw material cost linked to crude/petrochemical inputs not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: US formulations business accounted for 36% of FY25 global sales (primarily USD-denominated); Developed Markets (Europe/Canada/Australia) added 13% and other Emerging Markets 11% in local/other currencies. Specific hedging policy (forwards/natural hedge) not found in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin has publicly referenced India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs as an industry tailwind and has been expanding API capacity, but no confirmation was found of Lupin as an approved beneficiary receiving PLI disbursements (approved bulk-drug PLI beneficiary lists identified in searches did not confirm Lupin by name).

rural.evidence: Industry-level commentary indicates rural/semi-urban India drives ~60% of national gold consumption and Tanishq is targeting 130+ new small towns over 5 years; company-specific rural revenue % not disclosed in sources found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Titan's dominant raw material is gold bullion (jewellery ~88% of sales), not crude-oil linked. Company reported to follow a near-100% gold hedging strategy via gold-on-lease and forward contracts, among the highest in the industry.

rural.evidence: Company markets TMT bars for housing/construction; industry-wide commentary notes construction & real estate account for ~60% of India's steel consumption, but no company-specific rural revenue split found.

govt_capex.evidence: Company positions TMT/long products/flat steel business against a backdrop of record government infrastructure capex; industry sources note govt capital spending on infra at record levels for three straight years, driving TMT bar demand. No company-specific % disclosed in sources found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party summaries describe Shyam Metalics as 'almost debt free'; specific floating-rate liability disclosure not found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are iron ore, coal, and ferro-alloy inputs; not directly crude-oil linked.

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics (Flat Products) reported as selected to invest under the Ministry of Steel's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel; incentive/revenue contribution amount not found in sources reviewed (scheme disbursals for steel PLI reportedly begin FY2026-27).

china_plus_one.evidence: Granules is described as dependent on China for key starting material imports (e.g., DCDA, PAP), the reverse of a 'benefiting from clients diversifying away from China' narrative. Company has commissioned a DCDA pilot plant (~8,000 MT capacity) to reduce this China import dependency, which is a raw-material self-sufficiency initiative rather than an export-side China+1 win.

crude_exposure.evidence: API/pharma intermediate manufacturing uses petrochemical-derived solvents whose costs move with crude oil per industry commentary; Granules-specific quantification not found in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: ~94% of FY25 revenue from exports (North America ~77%, Europe ~5%), predominantly USD-denominated; sourced from a brokerage/press summary, not the AR directly.

pli_scheme.evidence: Granules India is a participant in the Government of India's PLI scheme for bulk drug intermediates/KSMs, with a committed 8,000 MT DCDA production capacity under the scheme; specific revenue/incentive contribution not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Reported in market commentary: 'Sai Life Sciences has reported unprecedented demand from Big Pharma clients diversifying away from China,' framed as a beneficiary of BIOSECURE Act-driven CDMO diversification from Chinese suppliers (alongside peers Jubilant Pharmova, Laurus Labs, Neuland Labs, Divi's Labs, Akums Drugs). Sourced from press/market summaries, not verified against the AR MD&A directly.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company used IPO proceeds to repay ~Rs 720 crore of debt in FY25, moving Net Debt/Equity from 0.84x (FY22) to approximately -0.04x (FY25) and eliminating an estimated ~Rs 85 crore annual interest cost — indicating materially reduced rate sensitivity post-listing. Precise floating-rate share of remaining liabilities not found.

inr_exposure.evidence: CRDMO business serves 280+/300+ innovator pharma and biotech customers across the US, UK, Europe and Japan (CDMO ~63% / CRO ~37% of FY25 revenue), implying predominantly foreign-currency revenue, but no precise USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosure found.
